data.title: mTOR regulates memory CD8 T-cell differentiation
data.authors: Araki K; Ahmed R et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: mTOR is a key regulator of memory CD8 T-cell differentiation; rapamycin enhances memory responses.
data.abstract_excerpt: Memory CD8 T cells are a critical component of protective immunity, and inducing effective memory T-cell responses is a major goal of vaccines against chronic infections and tumours. Considerable effort has gone into designing vaccine regimens that will increase the magnitude of the memory response, but there has been minimal emphasis on developing strategies to improve the functional qualities of memory T cells.

extracted_findings.effect: mTOR regulates memory CD8 T-cell differentiation; rapamycin enhances memory T-cell quantity and quality
extracted_findings.dose: Rapamycin administered continuously (day -1~35), during expansion (days -1~8), or contraction (days 8~35) post-infection; specific quantitative dose not stated.
extracted_findings.effect_size: Rapamycin enhanced LCMV-specific CD8 T cell responses, decreased T cell contraction, and improved functional qualities of memory CD8 T cells. Memory T cell numbers remained 10-fold higher even 165 days after stopping drug treatment, and rapamycin treatment during contraction resulted in significantly higher numbers of functional memory cells (p <0.0001~0.0022).
extracted_findings.limitations: mTOR knockdown does not completely mimic rapamycin treatment.
